column1: # Behaviour rules for --deep scanning.
# Tab-separated:  weight <TAB> category <TAB> regex <TAB> plain-English description
# Both scanners read this one file, so Windows and Linux cannot drift apart.
# Lines starting with # are comments. Blank lines are ignored.
# WRITING RULES
#   Regexes are matched case-insensitively against text that has already been
#   lowercased, de-obfuscated and (where applicable) base64-decoded.
#   Use only the regex subset that GNU grep -E and .NET both understand:
#     NOT   [[:space:]]  [[:alpha:]]  (?i)  lookbehind
#   POSIX bracket classes work in grep but NOT in .NET, so they are banned.
#   Descriptions are shown to frightened non-technical people. Say what the
#   script DOES, not what the technique is called. "hides its own window",
#   not "WindowStyle Hidden evasion".
# SCORING
#   A file is reported when   total score >= 6   AND   >= 2 distinct categories.
#   The two-category rule is what keeps false positives down: one loud signal
#   is not enough, the file has to look suspicious in more than one way.
#   Weights, roughly:
#     3 = strongly abnormal for a script sitting in someone's Documents folder
#     2 = notable
#     1 = common in legitimate scripts, only meaningful alongside others
